decisions.quote: In this section, we report on a reproduction of the study conducted by Brennan et al. (2012) using its methods and corpus, the Extended Brennan-Greenstadt corpus.
decisions.reason: This paper conducts both a reproduction using the original study's Extended Brennan-Greenstadt corpus and a separate replication using a newly collected corpus (the Riddell-Juola corpus). Because the blind coding schema allows only a single record_type per paper, the blind coder classified the paper as a replication while also retaining the reproduction axes. Shipped row 1349 from the reproductions source validly records the reproduction study of Brennan et al. (2012) on the original data.

decisions.quote: The chosen polynomial SVM has an average accuracy of 82.1% in attributing authorship given 40 candidates (the largest candidate-pool size in our settings; 10-fold cross-validation)—virtually identical to the accuracy reported in the original study.
decisions.reason: After reconstructing the Writeprints-static feature set and polynomial SVM on the original Extended Brennan-Greenstadt corpus, the authors obtain baseline cross-validation accuracy virtually identical to the original study (82.1% at 40 candidates) and recover the original defensive-strategy patterns in Figure 1. Under the codebook, obtaining the reported numbers via reconstructed steps qualifies as computationally reproducible, and the blind coder's cannot_be_determined establishes no error.

decisions.quote: The left panel of Figure 1 shows classifier accuracy on the training data measured using 10-fold cross-validation. The middle and right panels show the accuracy of the authorship attribution classifier when the subject uses the indicated defensive strategy. As we saw in the original paper, classifier performance drops dramatically when either defensive strategy is used, and the imitation strategy is more successful than the obfuscation strategy at confusing the Writeprints-static-based SVM classifier.
decisions.reason: In re-analyzing the original Extended Brennan-Greenstadt corpus, the authors also evaluate two alternative authorship attribution specifications (Koppel-512 function words with logistic regression and a pretrained RoBERTa model), reporting that performance is roughly similar to the Writeprints-static SVM model and that classifier accuracy drops substantially under both defensive strategies across Figure 1. The substantive finding on the original data holds across these alternative specifications, supporting 'robust'.
